principles: Customer authentication policy is scoped to the ACME LOS customer group, not Okta Everyone.
App access policy is assigned only to ACME LOS web and mobile apps.
Password material, security-question answers, and OTPs stay in Okta.
Backend profile sync happens only after a fresh ACME session.

hierarchy.label: Org Authenticators
hierarchy.purpose: Activate or disable the Okta authenticators the customer policies can reference.

hierarchy.label: Customer Group
hierarchy.purpose: Holds self-service ACME LOS customer users and keeps customer policy away from admin users.

hierarchy.label: Profile Enrollment
hierarchy.purpose: Registers new customers and targets them into the customer group.

hierarchy.label: Authenticator Enrollment
hierarchy.purpose: Requires the customer authenticators needed for sign-in and recovery.

hierarchy.label: Global Session
hierarchy.purpose: Controls customer Okta session lifetime and remember-device behavior.

hierarchy.label: App Sign-In
hierarchy.purpose: Controls ACME LOS web/mobile app sign-in and risk-based step-up.

hierarchy.label: Authorization Server
hierarchy.purpose: Issues ACME claims and tokens for scoped customer app access.

hierarchy.label: Account Management
hierarchy.purpose: Controls sensitive self-service account operations such as recovery and email/phone changes.

hierarchy.label: ACME Backend Sync
hierarchy.purpose: Syncs mutable profile data only after Okta has re-authenticated the user.

configures: custom authorization server access for ACME apps
token rule 'ACME LOS Default Tokens' scoped to {customerGroupName}
lead_id and customer_id claims for ID/access tokens
forgot email, forgot phone, forgot password, and account unlock recovery requirements
security-question challenge/hint plus the expected OTP proof
change email requires other-factor OTP plus security-question challenge/hint
change password requires current password plus factor proof and security-question challenge/hint
change phone requires email OTP plus security-question challenge/hint
fresh ACME sign-in after sensitive change

scenarios.title: New Customer Registration
flow: Customer starts Okta hosted registration from ACME app.
Profile enrollment registers the user and targets {customerGroupName}.
Authenticator enrollment requires password, email, and security question.
Phone remains disabled until ACS SMS is approved and enabled.
securityNotes: Admin users should not be members of {customerGroupName}.
Registration policy must not be scoped to Okta Everyone.

scenarios.title: Standard Sign-In
flow: Customer signs in through ACME LOS web or mobile OIDC app.
Global session policy applies to {customerGroupName}.
App access policy enforces password-first standard access.
Authorization server issues ACME claims for the scoped customer app session.
securityNotes: Browser receives only the opaque ACME session cookie.
Okta tokens remain server-side in the ACME session store.

scenarios.title: High-Risk Sign-In
flow: Okta evaluates the app sign-in risk rule.
High-risk access requires password-first 2FA.
Standard access remains lower priority.
securityNotes: Bootstrap logs a warning if the Okta org does not accept the adaptive risk rule.

scenarios.title: Forgot Email
flow: Customer chooses forgot email or lost email access from Okta-hosted recovery.
Okta verifies an alternate possession factor OTP such as phone/SMS when enabled.
Okta verifies the enrolled security-question challenge/hint.
Customer recovers the sign-in identifier or regains account access.
Customer must establish a fresh ACME sign-in before ACME syncs any profile data.
securityNotes: If phone/SMS is not approved yet, this scenario remains a documented target until another non-email recovery factor is enabled.
ACME never receives the security-question answer or OTP.
This scenario must be scoped to {customerGroupName}; admin users are out of scope.
oktaSurfaces: Security > Authenticators > Password > Rules > Recovery authenticators

scenarios.title: Forgot Password: Security Question + Email OTP
flow: Customer chooses forgot password from the Okta hosted sign-in page.
Okta account management or password recovery policy verifies the enrolled security-question challenge/hint.
Okta sends an email OTP or equivalent email recovery challenge before reset.
Customer sets a new password in Okta.
Okta signs the customer out or ACME treats any existing session as stale.
Customer must establish a fresh ACME sign-in with the new password.
securityNotes: ACME never receives the old password, new password, security-question answer, or email OTP.
This scenario must be scoped to {customerGroupName}; admin users are out of scope.
Until the Account Management API payload is finalized in bootstrap, confirm this in Okta Admin Console.
oktaSurfaces: Security > Authenticators > Password > Rules > Recovery authenticators

scenarios.title: Change Email
flow: Customer changes email in Okta-hosted account management.
Before the change is accepted, Okta requires other-factor OTP proof where available, not the email address being changed.
Okta verifies the enrolled security-question challenge/hint.
Okta signs the customer out or ACME treats the existing session as stale.
Customer signs in again with the new email.
ACME syncs backend email from the current Okta email claim when Okta subject is unchanged.
securityNotes: If phone/SMS is not approved yet, use another enrolled possession factor supported by the Okta org.
ACME logs the email-change event without logging old or new email values.

scenarios.title: Change Password
flow: Customer starts change password from Okta-hosted account management while signed in.
Okta verifies the current password.
Okta verifies a factor OTP and the security-question challenge/hint.
Customer sets the new password in Okta.
Okta signs the customer out or ACME treats the existing session as stale.
Customer signs in again with the new password.
securityNotes: ACME never receives old password, new password, security-question answer, or OTP.
The same active Okta session is not enough for ACME profile sync after the password change.

scenarios.title: Forgot Phone
flow: Customer reports lost phone or unavailable SMS factor through Okta-hosted recovery.
Okta verifies email OTP before allowing recovery to continue.
Okta verifies the enrolled security-question challenge/hint.
Customer signs in fresh and replaces the phone/SMS factor from account management.
ACME treats verified phone as Okta-owned until a trusted claim, Management API lookup, or event hook is enabled.
securityNotes: This scenario is not live until Okta phone/SMS is enabled or another non-phone possession factor is configured.
Do not use the unavailable phone factor as its own recovery proof.

scenarios.title: Change Phone/SMS
flow: Customer changes phone/SMS factor in Okta-hosted account management.
Okta requires email OTP before the phone/SMS factor is changed.
Okta verifies the enrolled security-question challenge/hint.
Okta signs the customer out or ACME treats the existing session as stale.
Customer signs in fresh after the phone/SMS change.
ACME treats verified phone as Okta-owned until a trusted profile claim, Management API lookup, or event hook is enabled.
securityNotes: Phone/SMS remains disabled until ACS toll-free verification is approved.
ACME does not claim an application servicing phone number is the verified Okta SMS factor.

scenarios.title: Fresh ACME Sign-In After Sensitive Change
flow: Sensitive Okta account-management action completes.
Existing ACME session is treated as stale for synced profile state.
Customer signs in again through the normal Okta redirect.
ACME syncs only non-secret profile data from fresh token claims.
securityNotes: Do not sync password material, OTPs, or security-question material.

scenarios.title: Customer ID Sample Writeback
flow: Customer saves ACME personal information.
Next validates the browser session and forwards trusted identity to the internal BFF.
BFF uses Okta Management OAuth service-app credentials to patch a sample customerId when missing.
Future sign-in receives the customerId claim from Okta.
securityNotes: Okta management private key is BFF-only through Key Vault or environment secret.
This sample bridge is dev-only until the real customer-id issuer exists.

manualChecks.title: Admin users are not in the ACME customer group
Forgot password requires security question plus email OTP and fresh sign-in
Email and phone account-management changes require the expected proofs
